newsitem.title: GERMANY: French and German officials arrive in Kempten.
newsitem.headline: French and German officials arrive in Kempten.

text.p: French and German officials have arrived in the Bavarian town of Kempten to continue talks expected to centre on economic developments and European economic and monetary union (EMU).

German Finance Minister Theo Waigel, Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer and Economics Minister Guenter Rexrodt were set to continue talks with French Finance Minister Jean Arthuis and Bank of France Governor Jean-Claude Trichet.

The officials arrived late because of bad weather which prevented them from landing at an airport near Kempten to start the talks at 0800 GMT. Instead, they had held an impromptu meeting in the Stuttgart airport VIP lounge.
Rexrodt arrived separately in Kempten just before the other officials, having landed at Memmingen airport near Kempten.
A news conference originally set for 1130 GMT was now expected to start at 1200 GMT.

As Waigel arrived in Kempten, he told reporters that he and Arthuis had discussed plans for a proposed stability pact to ensure lasting fiscal discipline among members of the single European currency after its launch.
They had also discussed preparations for an informal meeting of finance ministers in Dublin on Friday, Waigel said.
Other officials declined to comment on their talks so far.
"First we have to hold our meeting," Waigel told reporters.
